paper.title_en: Mass spectra of charged kaons and pions at finite magnetic field, temperature, and density
paper.abstract_en: The mass spectra of charged pions (<math display="inline"><msub><mi>π</mi><mo>±</mo></msub></math>) and kaons (<math display="inline"><msub><mi>K</mi><mo>±</mo></msub></math>) at finite magnetic field, temperature, and quark chemical potential are investigated in frame of a three-flavor Nambu–Jona–Lasinio model. Based on the analytical formula, we observe that different behavior between charged mesons and neutral mesons is induced by the isospin symmetry breaking in magnetic field, and different behavior between <math display="inline"><msub><mi>π</mi><mo>±</mo></msub></math> and <math display="inline"><msub><mi>K</mi><mo>±</mo></msub></math> mesons comes from different mass of constituent <math display="inline"><mi>u</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi></math> and <math display="inline"><mi>s</mi></math> quarks. With vanishing temperature and quark chemical potential, the mass of charged pions <math display="inline"><msub><mi>m</mi><msub><mi>π</mi><mo>+</mo></msub></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>m</mi><msub><mi>π</mi><mo>-</mo></msub></msub></math> and charged kaons <math display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi>m</mi></mrow><mrow><msub><mrow><mi>K</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>+</mo></mrow></msub></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mrow><mi>m</mi></mrow><mrow><msub><mrow><mi>K</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo></mrow></msub></mrow></msub></mrow></math> increase monotonically with magnetic field (<math display="inline"><mrow><mi>e</mi><mi>B</mi><mo><</mo><mn>40</mn><msubsup><mrow><mi>m</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>π</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow></math>). With fixed magnetic field and vanishing quark chemical potential, <math display="inline"><msub><mi>m</mi><msub><mi>π</mi><mo>+</mo></msub></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>m</mi><msub><mi>π</mi><mo>-</mo></msub></msub></math> and <math display="inline"><msub><mi>m</mi><msub><mi>K</mi><mo>+</mo></msub></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>m</mi><msub><mi>K</mi><mo>-</mo></msub></msub></math> show nonmonotonic behavior with increasing temperature, and several mass jumps at finite temperature caused by the discrete Landau level of constituent quarks. With fixed magnetic field and vanishing temperature, <math display="inline"><msub><mi>m</mi><msub><mi>π</mi><mo>+</mo></msub></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>m</mi><msub><mi>π</mi><mo>-</mo></msub></msub></math> and <math display="inline"><msub><mi>m</mi><msub><mi>K</mi><mo>+</mo></msub></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>m</mi><msub><mi>K</mi><mo>-</mo></msub></msub></math> remain constant at low-quark chemical potential, and then their mass jumps occur caused by the mass jump of constituent quarks. After that, <math display="inline"><msub><mi>m</mi><msub><mi>π</mi><mo>+</mo></msub></msub><mo>≃</mo><msub><mi>m</mi><msub><mi>π</mi><mo>-</mo></msub></msub></math> decreases with quark chemical potential, but <math display="inline"><msub><mi>m</mi><msub><mi>K</mi><mo>+</mo></msub></msub></math> (<math display="inline"><msub><mi>m</mi><msub><mi>K</mi><mo>-</mo></msub></msub></math>) first increases and then decreases (decreases monotonically) with quark chemical potential, with apparent mass deviation <math display="inline"><msub><mi>m</mi><msub><mi>K</mi><mo>+</mo></msub></msub><mo>≠</mo><msub><mi>m</mi><msub><mi>K</mi><mo>-</mo></msub></msub></math>. Furthermore, we consider the inverse magnetic catalysis (IMC) effect on meson mass spectra by using a magnetic field dependent coupling parameter <math display="inline"><mi>G</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>e</mi><mi>B</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math> in four-fermion interaction term <math display="inline"><msub><mi mathvariant="script">L</mi><mn>4</mn></msub></math> or a magnetic field dependent coupling parameter <math display="inline"><mi>K</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>e</mi><mi>B</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math> in six-fermion interaction term <math display="inline"><msub><mi mathvariant="script">L</mi><mn>6</mn></msub></math>. Including IMC effect does not lead to qualitative modification for the mass spectra at finite magnetic field, temperature, and quark chemical potential.
